text:
aj: Quick sync — I'm running a QA sweep comparing replay harness vs synthetic microburst generator. want to validate methodology before scaling to the full tenant matrix.

maria: 👍 share the config and the hypothesis you're testing

aj: Goal: measure fairness under short high-qps bursts and see how kernel selection + kv-cache prefetching changes tail latency and batch-size distribution. Hypothesis: microbursts expose unfairness when batch_cap>8 and max_delay_ms is tuned for throughput.

sara: can you post the exact harness flags?

aj: putting it here. this is the minimal job we run per-tenant:

```
mode: microburst_replay
workload: 95th-percentile-replay.json
burst_profile: { qps_peak: 1200, duration_ms: 200, interburst_ms: 500 }
batch_cap: [4,8,16]
max_delay_ms: [2,10,50]
kvcache.prefetch: [true,false]
kernel_policy: [auto, prefer-fp16, force-quant]
trace_level: perf+kv
```

kevin: nice. what's the tenant mix for the runs? single-tenant vs multi-tenant?

aj: runs include: single-tenant baseline, 4-tenants equal-weight, and skewed tenants (1 hot, 3 cold). each run = 15m stable window after warmup. we capture per-tenant batch-size histogram, per-token latency p50/p95/p99, kvcache hit ratio, and kernel-switch events.

maria: how do you define a kernel switch event in traces? sometimes small jitters look like switches

aj: we're using the runtime event: `kernel_selector.swap_to(<kernel_name>)` with a 10ms debounce. if two different kernel names appear within 10ms we count 1 switch (debounce to avoid noise).

bench-bot: automated: first 3 runs completed (batch_cap=4). aggregated: p99 latency increased 18% under skewed tenants; kv hit ratio stable. full logs: https://ci.internal/bench/1976543210/run1

sara: interesting. did you try disabling prefetch? prefetch can amplify cache pollution during bursts

aj: yes — early numbers: when prefetch=false and batch_cap=16, p99 for hot tenant drops 12% but cold tenants suffer +9% tail. tradeoff visible in per-tenant time series.

kevin: any weird kernel choices? auto policy selecting quant kernels during bursts?

aj: auto picked `quant_fast` for long sequences at high load in 2 runs — but we saw a regression: kernel swap frequency spiked and coincided with jitter spikes. suspect kernel selection cost > benefit under microburst churn.

maria: can you add an experiment: force-quant vs prefer-fp16 but with kernel_selector.swap_cost_ms artificially increased to simulate selector throttling?

aj: good call. will run adds: `selector.swap_cost_ms: [0,8,20]` and a control where we pin kernel by sequence length threshold.

ops-bot: FYI deploy-bot: new bench harness image pushed :bench: (sha: a1b2c3).

aj: also logging a minor perf regression note — on two runs with batch_cap=8, max_delay_ms=10, kernel_policy=auto, p95 increased vs baseline by ~7% after a runtime change last week. Need to bisect the kernel selection patch.

sara: if you can reproduce locally, we can instrument the selector path and add counters for candidate scoring time. small CPU overhead there could explain the extra latency under bursts.

aj: plan: run the new selector.swap_cost_ms matrix across tenant mixes, capture: per-tenant p99, kernel switch rate, avg batch_size, kv-hit, and selector cpu ms. will post a short summary thread with plots. aim to finish runs by EOD.

maria: thanks — lmk if you want help parsing the traces, I have some scripts to align kernel events with batch boundaries.

aj: appreciated. ping me if you want the run links. I'll post aggregated CSV + a perf notebook after runs. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ci-bot: scan complete — no infra alerts during runs.

aj: closing loop — opened a tracking issue for the regression: https://issues.internal/RED-8932. tagging kevin + sara.

kevin: great. if the selector is the culprit we might prefer a bounded-swap policy for microburst-prone queues.

maria: agree. keep notes short in the issue and include the per-tenant breakdown. thanks everyone. :slightly_smiling_face:
